title: Triage sprint — KPI entropy notes
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick scratchpad for the small, messy bits that are drifting our personal KPI signal. Trying to force a 2-week triage sprint to reduce metric entropy (too many one-off experiments, heatmap is noisy). This is intentionally informal — notes, half-formed hypotheses, and concrete tiny bets I can finish in a week.

Sprint window: 2025-10-06 -> 2025-10-19 (two weeks)
Primary focus: reduce noise in weekly active metric reporting and align my tasks to 3 clear results.

Draft Objective (personal): Reduce KPI entropy so weekly signals are actionable and lead to one follow-up every week.
KR draft (working):
- KR1: Trim backlog of “one-off” experiments from 12 -> 4 (definition: experiments without a PR, eval, or clear owner after 2 weeks).
- KR2: Move 80% of small metric changes into documented experiment templates (sheet + ticket) before running.
- KR3: Increase weekly follow-ups that lead to a decision (ship/kill/repeat) from 20% -> 50%.

Why this matters (short):
- I keep starting small A/Bish things (query tweaks, prompt params) and then forget to record. Results leak into dashboards as noise and we chase ghosts.
- If I can make the workflow mechanical (template + ticket), downstream teams (console, SRE) will have a clearer line of sight and fewer false alarms.

Current friction points (brainstorming):
- No quick template for tiny experiments — I use 3 different sheets or a scratch GH issue.
- Lack of guardrail for running “playful” prompt experiments: they end up in production variances.
- Weekly check-in is too high level; micro-decisions are lost between demos and retros.
- I defer creating PRs for micro-experiments (low priority) -> results never land in main repo/evals.

Small bets (concrete tasks):
1) Make a 1-page experiment template (sheet + one-click copy link) and a Micro-Experiment label in Jira. (Estimate: 1–2 hours). Ticket: PS-1423 (linked).
2) Triage backlog: go through my 12 dangling experiments, classify: keep / document / kill. Aim to close or document 8 this sprint. (Estimate: 4–6 hours).
3) Run a test of the template: pick 2 experiments, follow the template, open PR or eval artifact. Measure time-to-document. (Estimate: 3 hours).
4) Weekly check-in tweak: add a 3-line micro-followup row in my weekly notes and ping owner. Track followups in a tiny sheet. (Estimate: 30m to set up; 15m each week).

Hypotheses to validate (H1..H3):
H1: Having a 1-click template will increase documentation rate from ~20% -> >70% for experiments under 2 days.
H2: Classifying backlog will reveal at least 4 experiments that are duplicates or obsolete (i.e., no longer relevant given model changes).
H3: Adding a micro-followup row in weekly notes will double the number of decisions recorded within 7 days.

Success signals (binary / quantitative):
- Success if documented experiments > 80% of trials in sprint window.
- Success if backlog of undocumented experiments <= 4.
- Better signal: at least one consumer (product/console) calls out clearer dashboards in next sync. (soft).

Measurement plan (where I will track):
- Tiny sheet: columns = experiment id, owner, date started, linked PR/eval, status (documented/undocumented/killed), followup deadline.
- Weekly note: micro-followup table with columns [what, owner, decision-by, outcome].
- Quick query to usage dashboard: count of metric blips tagged to my experiments (manual mapping initially).

Triage rubric (quick):
- If experiment < 2% expected impact and > 1 week stale -> kill.
- If experiment reproducible and > 5% delta on a core metric -> escalate to a proper A/B ticket + PR.
- If unclear: document and set a 1-week decision deadline.

Sample micro-experiment (how I’ll fill the template):
- Title: reduce-cache-prefix-length for small requests
- Hypothesis: shorter prefixes will reduce tokenization overhead for embedding lookups -> 4–6% latency improvement for 95p latency.
- Metric: 95p latency on /v1/embeddings-proxy for small sequence workloads (internal dashboard).
- Timebox: 3 days. Owner: me. Action: modify patch, run small eval harness, record results, open PR or mark kill.

Backlog triage notes (quick run):
- prompt-tempo-sweep: undocumented, last run 2025-08-22 -> document and set decision-by 2025-10-12
- cache-prefix-length: partial notes only -> run micro-experiment (see above)
- batch-window-sample: has PR but no eval artifact -> attach eval + close
- client-retry-tweak: small change pushed without ticket -> open kill/confirm ticket
- temperature-range-tiles: duplicate of prompt-tempo-sweep -> kill (merge notes)
- token-budget-heuristic: needs more context, move to documented queue
- lazy-load-kv-cache: abandoned proof-of-concept -> kill
- routing-weight-probe: small telemetry present -> document + set decision-by
- embedding-dedup-flow: needs owner -> ping @Ravi for handoff

Retrospective items (from last two sprints):
- Good: quick experiments produced surprising wins (2 small wins that became inputs to Optimize).
- Bad: several experiments never had follow-up and popped up as oddities in dashboards -> noise.
- Pattern: I prefer iterating quickly but lack the discipline to finish the metadata step.

Immediate next actions (this afternoon):
- Create a copyable template in Drive (file: Micro-Experiment Template (v0.1)).
- Create Jira label and make PS-1423 the parent ticket for backlog triage.
- Triage the top 6 backlog items and note decisions in the tiny sheet.

Questions / unresolved:
- Should micro-experiments always create a PR? (costly for 30-min tests) -> maybe only if result leads to a code path change or will affect dashboards.
- What’s the minimal eval artifact needed to consider an experiment documented? Raw numbers in sheet + short note? Or must include a reproducible script/eval harness?

Notes to self (style reminders):
- Prefer "document-first" — documenting the intent before running reduces bias.
- If a two-hour exploration looks promising, create a ticket before continuing.
- Keep the template lean: title, hypothesis, metric(s), timebox, owner, link-to-artifact, decision-by.

Slack nudge drafts to post after triage: 
"Quick heads-up — tidying my micro-experiment backlog this week. If you own any of the items in the sheet I’ll ping you for a short decision (ship/kill/document)."

Log of small timings (for planning):
- Template + label + sheet: 45m
- Triage top 6: 1.5–2h
- Run 2 experiments following template: 3h total

Finish note: make the habit mechanical. If I can turn the friction into a 1-click copy + 5 field form, I should be able to maintain a low-noise dashboard and run faster, safer bets.

-- emma
